# Every operation

<!-- generated by scripts/openapi_pages.py from docs/openapi.json: don't edit by hand -->

The 22 operations of PGP Chat Bot API 1.0.0, as the server's OpenAPI document describes them. All paths are under `{apiUrl}/bot/v1`. Every call needs the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and every answer is the envelope `{"ok": true, "result": ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": {...}}`.

The SDK column links to the method that runs the operation. It has the same name on `AsyncClient`, `Client`, `Bot` and `SyncBot`.

## `GET /me`

**Who the bot is**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `getMe` |
| Tag | Me |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.get_me` |

The bot's own card as the server holds it, plus the limits this server enforces. This works while the bot is paused, so a programme can find out why nothing else does.

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | The bot. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `GET /updates`

**Fetch updates (long polling)**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `getUpdates` |
| Tag | Updates |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.get_updates` |

Returns the updates waiting for the bot, oldest first, up to `limit`. With `timeout` the call hangs until something arrives or the clock runs out, and answers an empty list on the clock.

`offset` confirms: every update with an `updateId` below it is deleted and never shown again. Send the highest `updateId` you handled plus one. Without `offset` you get everything still in the queue, which is what a bot asks on its very first call.

Only one poll per bot at a time. A second call ends the first one at once with an empty answer, so two copies of the same programme polling one bot will starve each other: run one.

Not available while a webhook is set: delete the webhook first.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | query | integer | no | min `0` | Confirm everything below this id. Highest handled `updateId` + 1. |
| `limit` | query | integer | no | min `1`; max `100` | At most this many, 1 to 100. Default 100. |
| `timeout` | query | integer | no | min `0`; max `50` | Seconds to wait for something to arrive, 0 to 50. Default 0. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Updates, oldest first. Empty when nothing arrived before the timeout. |
| `400` | `bad_request`: the body or the query is wrong; `message` says which field. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `409` | A webhook is set. Delete it before polling. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `POST /webhook`

**Set a webhook**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `setWebhook` |
| Tag | Updates |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.set_webhook` |

From now on every update is POSTed as JSON to `url`, one update per request, in order, with the header `User-Agent: PGPChat-Bot-Api/1`. If you give a `secret`, every delivery carries it in the header `X-PGPChat-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`: check it and refuse anything without it.

Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds and the update is considered delivered. Anything else, a timeout or a redirect counts as a failure: the server backs off (one second, then doubling, up to an hour) and tries that same update again, so delivery is at least once and never out of order. After ten failures in a row the owner is told in the app. Updates still queue while the webhook is failing and are kept for 72 hours.

The URL must be `https`, carry no credentials or fragment, and resolve to a public address. Setting a webhook ends any poll in progress; `GET /updates` refuses while one is set.

Request body (JSON, required):

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | max length `1024` | Absolute https URL. |
| `secret` | string | no | pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,256}$` | Sent back on every delivery in `X-PGPChat-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Set. |
| `400` | The URL is not acceptable (`bad_webhook`) or the body is wrong (`bad_request`). |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `PUT /key`

**Publish the bot's OpenPGP public key**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `setKey` |
| Tag | Key |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.set_key` |

Turns the bot *protected*: from now on its private chats are end-to-end encrypted, people's phones seal every message to this key, and the bot must send `armored` into those chats. Calling it again with a new key is a rotation; every phone learns the new fingerprint at once.

There is no way to remove the key from the API on purpose: downgrading a bot from protected to open is a decision for its owner, in the console.

Request body (JSON, required):

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `publicKey` | string | yes | max length `65536` | ASCII-armoured OpenPGP public key block. |
| `fingerprint` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9A-Fa-f]{40}$\|^[0-9A-Fa-f]{64}$` | The key's fingerprint, 40 (v4) or 64 (v6) hex characters. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Published. |
| `400` | `bad_request`: the body or the query is wrong; `message` says which field. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `PUT /commands`

**Replace the commands of one scope**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `setCommands` |
| Tag | Commands |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.set_commands` |

The whole list of that scope, replaced. Up to 100 commands; a command is 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and underscores (a leading slash is dropped), its description 1 to 256 characters. Duplicates are folded to the first.

Scopes resolve the way Telegram's do, narrowest first: in a private chat `private` then `default`; in a group `chat:<id>`, then `groupAdmins` for administrators, then `groups`, then `default`. An empty scope does not hide a wider one. The owner can edit the same lists in the console; whichever wrote last wins.

Request body (JSON, required):

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | string | no | pattern `^(default\|private\|groups\|groupAdmins\|chat:\d{1,12})$` | `default`, `private`, `groups`, `groupAdmins`, or `chat:<id>` for one chat the bot is in. Missing means `default`. |
| `commands` | array of object | yes |  |  |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Saved. |
| `400` | `bad_request`: the body or the query is wrong; `message` says which field. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `404` | A `chat:<id>` scope names a chat the bot is not in. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `POST /messages`

**Send a message**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `sendMessage` |
| Tag | Messages |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.send_message` |

Into a chat the bot is in. Send `text` into a readable chat and `armored` into an encrypted one; the wrong kind is refused with `wrong_body_kind` and `expected` says which. A `markup` adds rows of buttons under the message. `replyTo` quotes a message of the same chat (a wrong id is silently dropped). `silent` only matters in a channel: the post goes out without a notification.

`sendId` makes the call safe to repeat: a UUID of your choosing, and a second call with the same one hands back the message already written instead of writing it twice. Use it whenever you retry after a timeout.

In an encrypted chat, seal the message to every key `GET /chats/{id}/keys` returns and to the bot's own key, sign it with the bot's key, and send the armoured result.

Request body (JSON, required):

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chatId` | integer | yes |  |  |
| `text` | string | no | min length `1`; max length `4096` | Readable chats. No control characters apart from newline and tab. |
| `armored` | string | no | max length `131072` | Encrypted chats. An ASCII-armoured OpenPGP message. |
| `replyTo` | integer or null | no |  |  |
| `markup` | object | no |  | Rows of buttons under a message. Up to 20 rows, 8 buttons a row, 100 in all, 8 KiB of JSON. The buttons are not encrypted: the server has to know which one was pressed. |
| `silent` | boolean | no |  | Channels only: no notification. |
| `sendId` | string | no | format `uuid` | Your id for this send, so a retry writes nothing twice. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `201` | Sent. A repeated `sendId` answers 200 with the message already written instead of writing it twice. |
| `400` | `bad_request`, `wrong_body_kind` (with `expected`) or `bad_markup`. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`, `user_gone` (the person closed their account), `blocked_by_user`, or `forbidden` (no right to write here). |
| `404` | `chat_not_found`: no such chat, or the bot is not in it. |
| `409` | `conflict`: this `sendId` was already used in another chat. |
| `429` | `flood_wait` (sending too fast), `slow_mode` (the group's slow mode) or `rate_limited`. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `PATCH /messages/{messageId}`

**Edit one of the bot's messages**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `editMessage` |
| Tag | Messages |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.edit_message` |

New words, new buttons, or both. Only the bot's own ordinary messages, at any age: a scoreboard that changes for a week is the normal use. Service notices the bot caused ("left the group") are not its to edit. Leave `markup` out to keep the buttons, send `markup: null` to remove them. People in the chat see the edit live. Edits are counted against the same numbers as sends, in a window of their own: one a second in a private chat, twenty a minute in a group, and the thirty a second overall is shared.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `messageId` | path | integer | yes |  |  |

Request body (JSON, required):

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chatId` | integer | yes |  |  |
| `text` | string | no | max length `4096` |  |
| `armored` | string | no | max length `131072` |  |
| `markup` | object or null | no |  | Omit to keep the buttons, `null` to remove them. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Edited. |
| `400` | `bad_request` (nothing to change, or a field is wrong), `wrong_body_kind` (`text` into an encrypted chat or `armored` into a readable one, see `expected`) or `bad_markup`. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `forbidden`: not the bot's message, or not an ordinary one. In a private chat `blocked_by_user` or `user_gone`. `bot_paused`. |
| `404` | `chat_not_found` or `message_not_found`. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `POST /callbacks/{callbackId}/answer`

**Answer a button press**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `answerCallback` |
| Tag | Buttons |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.answer_callback` |

When somebody presses a button with `callbackData`, the bot gets a `callback_query` update and the button spins on their phone. Answer within 60 seconds: with `text` a short line flashes over the chat; with `alert: true` the text is shown in a box they have to dismiss; with `url` their phone shows the address and offers to open it. An empty answer just stops the spinner. The message itself changes only if you edit it (`PATCH /messages/{id}`).

Each press is answered once. A second press on the same message while the first is open is the same press.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `callbackId` | path | string | yes |  |  |

Request body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | no | max length `200` |  |
| `alert` | boolean | no | default `false` |  |
| `url` | string | no | max length `1024` | Absolute http(s) URL without credentials. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Delivered to the phone that pressed. |
| `400` | `bad_request`: the body or the query is wrong; `message` says which field. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `404` | `callback_not_found`: no such press for this bot. |
| `409` | `callback_answered`: already answered. |
| `410` | `callback_expired`: more than 60 seconds have passed. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `POST /chats/{chatId}/typing`

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `sendTyping` |
| Tag | Chats |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.send_typing` |

The same indicator a person's phone sends. It clears on its own after a few seconds or when a message lands; send `typing: false` to clear it early. | `typing` | boolean | no | default `true` |  |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | `sent` is false when one went out to this chat less than 3 seconds ago. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `forbidden`: the bot may not write in this chat. `bot_paused`. |
| `404` | `chat_not_found`: no such chat, or the bot is not in it. |

## `GET /resolve/{username}`

**A public handle, turned into an id**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `resolve` |
| Tag | Names |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.resolve` |

For the handle a person types at your bot - "paga @anna", "segui @notizie" - when no message has handed you that id. People, groups and channels share one pool of names, so a handle is held by exactly one of the three and `kind` says which.

The answer carries `id` at the top, and the same thing again under `user` or `chat` with what little goes with it. `username` is the name that account or chat actually goes by, which is not always the one you asked with: a person can answer to several handles.

It finds anybody with a public handle, which is no more than the short link already tells a stranger with a browser (`pgpchat.me/anna`). The id on its own grants nothing: sending still needs the bot to be in the chat, and a key still needs a chat in common. Out of reach: a chat with no public name (a private group is not in the pool at all), an account that has been closed, and the server's own service account.

Harder limit than the rest of the API: 60 a minute, and a handle nobody holds counts as five, so about a dozen blind guesses spend the minute. Over it you get `429 flood_wait` with `retryAfter`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | path | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,32}$` | A public handle, without the `@`. 3-32 characters: letters, digits and underscore. Case does not matter. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | What the handle turned out to be. |
| `400` | `bad_request`: the body or the query is wrong; `message` says which field. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `404` | `username_not_found`: nobody and no chat answers to that name. |
| `429` | `flood_wait`: too many lookups, wait `retryAfter` seconds. `rate_limited`. |

## `GET /users/{userId}/key`

**One person's public key**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `getUserKey` |
| Tag | Chats |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.get_user_key` |

Only for somebody the bot shares a chat with; anybody else is `user_not_found`, whether or not they exist.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `userId` | path | integer | yes |  |  |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | The key. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `403` | `bot_paused`: the owner paused the bot. Only `GET /me`, `GET /webhook`, `DELETE /webhook` and `POST /token/revoke` work meanwhile. |
| `404` | `user_not_found` or `no_user_key`. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## `POST /token/revoke`

**Burn this token**

| | |
|---|---|
| operationId | `revokeToken` |
| Tag | Token |
| SDK | {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.AsyncClient.revoke_token` |

For a programme that notices its token leaked. Nothing works again, this call included, until the owner issues a new token in the console; the owner is told at once. Works while paused.

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Revoked. |
| `401` | `unauthorized`: missing, revoked or invalid token. |
| `429` | `rate_limited`: too many calls. Wait `retryAfter` seconds. |

## Webhook: `update`

**An update, delivered to your webhook**

One update per request, in order. Answer any 2xx within 10 seconds. The header `X-PGPChat-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` carries the secret you set, if any; `User-Agent` is `PGPChat-Bot-Api/1`. Deliveries are at least once: a slow 2xx can be retried, so treat `updateId` as the thing that makes a delivery new.

The body is one `Update`. In the SDK: {py:meth}`~pgpcbot.Bot.create_webhook_app`.

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Any 2xx: delivered. Anything else, a timeout or a redirect: retried later. |
